adjustments.change: Strengthen missing-target search from a preference for different already-checked candidates to a concrete next-move rule: choose an admissible candidate not in the current location or the last two visited locations, prefer an uninspected candidate, use the next same-type instance or a different type after an empty container, and include plausible large surfaces and the named destination surface as candidates. Preserve the known-target-instance return exception as an override of the recent-location exclusion for both single- and multi-instance tasks.
adjustments.reason: Current `P3` and `P6` (group `G2`) show the original gap remains severe: `P3` repeatedly revisits fridge 1, countertop 1/2, cabinet 1, and drawer 1/2 while leaving diningtable 1/2 and most other cabinets/drawers unvisited, ending at `P3:outcome` with step_limit; `P6` repeatedly revisits shelf 1/2, drawer 1-4, desk 1, and sidetable 1 while never checking bed 1, garbagecan 1, or drawers 5/6, ending at `P6:outcome` with step_limit. Historical `M2` reports a paired candidate failure at `S1_R02/Q8:50` even after broadened search guidance and without visiting diningtable 1; `M4` reports failed search loops at `S1_R04/Q5:50`; `M5` reports a less efficient candidate cycle at `S1_R05/Q10:19`. This supports the same direction but shows generic 'prefer different' language and container-only expansion were insufficient. The strengthened recent-history exclusion, sequential same-type instance choice, and explicit inclusion of large surfaces/destination surface directly address these observable coverage gaps. The last-two-pair trigger and destination-surface inclusion are unverified implementation choices, balanced by the preserved known-target return exception and by not forbidding returns when no unchecked candidate is available. The revised `c1` tests this added surface/destination coverage and recent-history exclusion, not just general anti-revisit behavior.

--- a/SKILL.md
+++ b/SKILL.md
@@
 - When a task's required target is missing because it is neither visible nor held, do not repeatedly cycle among the same small set of already-checked locations; after a checked location yields no target, choose a different candidate location for the next move.
-- Prefer a candidate that is not shown as already checked in the recent observations; when the current or recent location is an empty container, prefer the next unexamined instance of the same container type or a different visible container/surface type before returning to the same checked set.
-- Apply this missing-target search expansion to both single-instance and multi-instance target tasks, not only while a multi-instance task remains unmet.
-- Do not repeatedly alternate between two or more already-checked locations; each missing-target move should search a not-yet-recently-checked candidate or open a newly reached closed container while plausible candidates remain.
-- Preserve the existing collection exception: when a known location still contains a needed target instance, return to it as required by the collection guidance rather than avoiding it solely because it was previously visited.
+- On the next search move, choose an admissible candidate that is not the current location and not one of the locations visited in the last two pre-action observation/action pairs; when a candidate not yet inspected in those observations is available, choose it rather than a recently checked location.
+- If the current or recent location is an empty container, choose an admissible instance of the same container type whose name is not in the recent history when available, or a different visible container/surface type before returning to the same checked set.
+- Include all plausible visible surfaces and furniture in the candidate set, such as dining tables, desks, beds, sidetables, countertops, shelves, and the named destination surface, as well as remaining closed containers; do not assume the target cannot be on the destination surface.
+- Apply this missing-target search expansion to both single-instance and multi-instance target tasks, not only while a multi-instance task remains unmet.
+- Do not repeatedly alternate between two or more already-checked locations; if the last two search moves were to already-checked locations and plausible unchecked candidates remain, choose an unchecked candidate or open a newly reached closed container from the admissible actions before any return to a checked location.
+- Preserve the existing collection exception: when a known location still contains a needed target instance, return to it as required by the collection guidance even if it appears in the recent history; this exception overrides the recent-location exclusion.
